name: Tiroler Landesmuseum Ferdinandeum
kurzbeschreibung: The Tyrolean State Museum Ferdinandeum in Innsbruck showcases celebrated collections spanning from the Stone Age to contemporary art.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Tyrolean State Museum Ferdinandeum (Tiroler Landesmuseum Ferdinandeum) in Innsbruck is the premier universal museum of Tyrol and one of Central Europe's grand cultural institutions. Named in honour of Crown Prince Ferdinand (later Emperor Ferdinand I), the museum was established in 1823 as a national treasury. Housed in an imposing neoclassical palace on Museumstraße, the museum curates seven specialized collections charting Tyrol's archaeology, history, natural science, and fine art from prehistoric times through the Gothic and Renaissance eras to contemporary modernism. Highlights include masterpiece paintings by Lucas Cranach the Elder, Michael Pacher, and Rembrandt, alongside an exquisite gallery of modern Tyrolean art featuring Albin Egger-Lienz and Max Weiler.

Route & Requirements

The museum galleries span several spacious floors connected by modern passenger lifts and wide staircases, ensuring full barrier-free access throughout. A clear chronological layout allows visitors to navigate seamlessly across historical epochs. Visitors should plan for at least two hours to properly explore the permanent collections and temporary exhibitions. The museum is climate-controlled and equipped with comfortable rest seating, tactile discovery points, and multilingual audio guides suited for all ages.

Visit & Arrival

The Ferdinandeum is located in central Innsbruck on Museumstraße, just a five-minute stroll from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof and the pedestrian old town. Numerous bus and tram lines stop nearby at Hauptbahnhof or Museumstraße. Drivers can park in nearby public underground garages such as City-Garage or Kaufhaus Tyrol. The museum is open year-round from Tuesday to Sunday (closed Mondays). Combined tickets grant discounted admission to all partner sites of the Tyrolean State Museums network.

Tips

Be sure to examine the celebrated musical instruments collection, showcasing authentic violins crafted by Jakob Stainer of Absam, known as the father of German violin making. Relax after your tour at the inviting museum café, or browse the art bookshop featuring publications on regional cultural history. The museum also stages acclaimed temporary exhibitions of international contemporary art and weekend workshops for families.
